description: Call Workers AI, AI Gateway catalog models, dynamic routes, and vendor models from the AI SDK or Pi AI with one createAI provider over the AI binding or an account id and API token.
title: Models
image: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/models/og.png?v=dd8074fab97f2bb3
---

[Skip to content](#main-content)

> Documentation Index  
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/llms.txt  
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Models

Last updated Oct 21, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](index.md)|[Agent setup](/agent-setup/)


## How a model is chosen

Name a model with a string, or pass a model object built by the vendor's own package:

```ts
ai("@cf/zai-org/glm-4.7-flash"); // Workers AI
ai("anthropic/claude-opus-5.5"); // AI Gateway catalog
ai("dynamic/support"); // AI Gateway dynamic route
ai(anthropic("claude-opus-5-5")); // the vendor's own model object
```

* **A Workers AI model** is a `@cf/` id. It runs through `env.AI.run()`. A compatibility layer turns each model's response into the standard OpenAI chat completions shape.
* **An AI Gateway catalog model** is an `<author>/<model>` id from the [model catalog](/ai/models/), such as `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5` or `openai/gpt-5.5`. It also runs through `env.AI.run()`, which sends it to AI Gateway. The gateway picks a provider and bills the call. Use the catalog's spelling, not the vendor's: `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5`, not `claude-opus-5-5`.
* **A [dynamic route](/ai-gateway/features/dynamic-routing/)** is `dynamic/<route>`. The route you configured on the gateway picks the model.
* **A model object** comes from the vendor's provider package, such as `anthropic("claude-opus-5-5")`. The vendor's code builds the request and parses the response. The provider sends that request unchanged through the binding to AI Gateway's [provider-native endpoint](/ai-gateway/usage/providers/) for that vendor.

The providers do not use the deprecated [Universal Endpoint](/ai-gateway/usage/universal/).

## What every model gets

Serves the default model, or a model folder or hf:// repo set # through PTTS_MODEL. # docker build -f ptts-openai-server/Dockerfile -t ptts-openai-server . FROM rust:1-bookworm AS build RUN apt-get update \ && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libopus-dev libmp3lame-dev pkg-config \ && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* WORKDIR /src COPY . . # `.cargo/config.toml` is left out of the build context (see Dockerfile.dockerignore), so nothing # pins `target-cpu=native`. x86_64 gets x86-64-v3, as the Python wheels do: `xn` picks its # quantized kernels at compile time, and a lower baseline would cost q8 its AVX kernels. Many # small home servers have no AVX2, so it also gets an x86-64-v2 build, and `select-cpu.sh` # starts whichever one the CPU can run. ARG TARGETARCH RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/usr/local/cargo/registry \ --mount=type=cache,target=/src/target,sharing=locked \ if [ "$TARGETARCH" = "amd64" ]; then \ for level in v3 v2; do \ RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=x86-64-$level" cargo build --release --locked \ -p ptts-openai-server --target-dir "target/x86-64-$level" \ && install -D "target/x86-64-$level/release/ptts-openai-server" \ "/out/libexec/ptts/ptts-openai-server-x86-64-$level" || exit 1; \ done \ && install -D ptts-openai-server/select-cpu.sh /out/bin/ptts-openai-server; \ else \ cargo build --release --locked -p ptts-openai-server \ && install -D target/release/ptts-openai-server /out/bin/ptts-openai-server; \ fi FROM debian:bookworm-slim RUN apt-get update \ && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates libmp3lame0 libopus0 \ && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \ && useradd --create-home --uid 1000 phonon \ && install -d -o phonon -g phonon /home/phonon/.cache /home/phonon/.cache/huggingface COPY --from=build /out/ /usr/local/ LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/gradium-ai/xn-ptts" \ org.opencontainers.image.description="OpenAI-compatible text-to-speech server for Phonon" USER phonon # Every flag has an environment variable (`--help` lists them), so `docker run -e PTTS_LANG=fr` # or a compose file's `environment:` configures the server. q8 because this image runs on the # CPU, where it is faster than f32. ENV HF_HOME=/home/phonon/.cache/huggingface \ PTTS_LANG=en \ PTTS_QUANT=q8 # 10200 is the Wyoming protocol, served only when PTTS_WYOMING_ADDR is set. EXPOSE 8880 10200 ENTRYPOINT ["ptts-openai-server"] ---DOCKERWF name: Docker # The `ptts-openai-server` image for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. Each platform builds on a # native runner, since compiling Rust under QEMU takes hours, and the two are joined into one # multi-platform tag. A pull request that touches the server builds both without pushing; a push # to main that changes what goes into the image pushes `main`; and a `v*` tag pushes the version, # and `latest` unless it is a pre-release. on: push: branches: [main] tags: ["v*"] # Not evaluated for tags, which always build. paths: - ptts/** - ptts-openai-server/** - Cargo.toml - Cargo.lock - .github/workflows/docker.yml pull_request: paths: - ptts-openai-server/** - .github/workflows/docker.yml workflow_dispatch: permissions: contents: read concurrency: group: docker-${{ github.ref }} cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }} env: IMAGE: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/ptts-openai-server PUSH: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }} jobs: build: name: Build ${{ matrix.platform }} runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }} timeout-minutes: 60 permissions: contents: read packages: write strategy: fail-fast: false matrix: include: - { platform: linux/amd64, runner: ubuntu-24.04, arch: amd64 } - { platform: linux/arm64, runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm, arch: arm64 } ---README 5:Phonon brings natural text-to-speech to phones, laptops, browsers, and local 13: 58: inside a mobile app or load in a browser tab. 61:- **Fast across devices:** A custom inference stack runs in browsers and on 64: deliver faster inference than Kokoro and llama.cpp-based runtimes on the same 75:second of compute (higher is faster; above 1x is faster than real time) and the time to first 87:- On one MacBook Air core, Phonon 40m reaches 20x real time with a 7 ms TTFB. Kokoro (82M), through 99:| [Run speech in a web app](#browser) | `phonon-tts` | [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/phonon-tts) | Worker, single-thread and threaded Wasm builds, and TypeScript declarations. [Browser guide](ptts-wasm/js/README.md). | 111:Without a model argument, the command line, Python, the browser package, the servers and Rust download the default model from Hugging Face on first use and cache it. The default is Phonon 31m, [`hf://gradium/phonon-31m-en`](https://huggingface.co/gradium/phonon-31m-en), pinned to one commit. Swift and Android load a model bundle you add to the app. 121:Phonon 31m is public. The Phonon 40m models are gated. To use one, accept its terms on its Hugging Face page; approval is automatic. Then set `HF_TOKEN` or run `hf auth login`, and the command line, Python, the servers and Rust download it like any other model. The browser package has no token to send, so it loads only Phonon 31m from Hugging Face. To use a Phonon 40m model in a browser, download its files and serve them with your app, under the model's license. 208:Use `--model` for another model (see [Model setup](#model-setup)), `--quant q8` for faster q8 weights on the CPU, and `--voice NAME` to choose a voice, from the model or the [voice catalog](#voices); omitting it uses the model's default voice. Run `ptts --help` for the remaining options. [CLI guide →](docs/cli.md) 253:### Browser 256:Show browser quickstart 258:Install the browser package into your web app: 275:The browser cannot load gated repos, so the Phonon 40m models load only from 280:[browser guide](ptts-wasm/js/README.md#streaming) includes a complete Web Audio 284:progress. Serve over HTTPS or localhost for caching, and use a browser with 285:WebAssembly SIMD. The package runs in browsers, not Node.js. CPU is the default. 286:Threading and WebGPU setup are covered in the [browser guide 287:→](ptts-wasm/js/README.md). 425:| [`offline-dino-game`](https://github.com/gradium-ai/examples/tree/main/offline-dino-game) | Phonon in the browser: a dino game where Rex roasts you as you play, every line spoken live in the tab. | ---DOCS "path": "docs/cli.md", "path": "docs/development.md", "path": "docs/readme", ---WASMSPEED 67:| `quant` | `'q8'` | `'q8'` (smaller, faster) or `'f32'` | 133:- A browser with WebAssembly SIMD and module workers. Browsers with Relaxed SIMD get a faster build; others, such as Safari and every browser on iOS, load one without it. A browser without SIMD cannot load the module, and `load` rejects with an error saying so. 136:How close to real time it gets depends on the device, on [WebGPU](#webgpu) and on [threads](#threads), and `q8` is noticeably faster than `f32`. 140:The model runs on the CPU unless asked otherwise. WebGPU is opt in, because it is not faster than the CPU on every device: on phones the threaded CPU build can beat it. Pass `device: 'webgpu'` to run on the GPU, and `load` rejects if it cannot start. Pass `device: 'auto'` to use the GPU when the browser hands out a WebGPU adapter and the weights are `q8` in a GGUF file, and the CPU otherwise. Under `'auto'` a software fallback adapter counts as none, since it would run slower than the CPU. `q8` weights go to the GPU as they are; other weights would have to be quantized there, which means reading each one back to the host, and a browser cannot wait for that. WebGPU needs no cross-origin isolation, and it works in the same secure contexts as the cache. Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp ``` With them, the page can only load cross-origin resources that opt in, through CORS or a `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy` header. That includes the model files, if they are served from another origin. The package ships two wasm builds, each with and without Relaxed SIMD, and picks one when it loads: the threaded build on an isolated page, the single-threaded one elsewhere, or if threads fail to start. Both produce the same audio. `tts.threads` says how many threads it got, and `tts.threadsReason` why. `'auto'` uses 3 threads, or fewer on a device with fewer cores: past a few threads, handing out the work costs more than it saves, and a thread that lands on an efficiency core slows the rest down. Pass `threads: 1` to stay on one thread, or a number of your own for devices you know better. This build speaks with ready-made voices only: cloning from an audio sample is not in the browser build. Voices from the catalog [`gradium/phonon-voices`](https://huggingface.co/gradium/phonon-voices) load with `addVoice` from the URL of their file, for example `await tts.addVoice('Zoey', 'https://huggingface.co/gradium/phonon-voices/resolve/main/voices/NbpkqMVS3CJeq2j8.safetensors')`. The catalog's `voices.jsonl` lists each voice's name, language and file. Voice files from the Gradium Studio scripts in the [repository](https://github.com/gradium-ai/xn-ptts#voices) load the same way. ## Licence The package is MIT OR Apache-2.0. Model weights are not part of it and come with their own licenses: Phonon 31m is under Apache 2.0, and Phonon 40m and Phonon 40m multilingual are under CC BY-NC 4.0. See each model's page on Hugging Face.

**SIMD:** Supported. The page says, "SIMD is supported on Workers."

**Threads, SharedArrayBuffer, atomics:** The page covers threading only. "Threading is not possible in Workers." It adds that "Each Worker runs in a single thread, and the Web Worker API is not supported." It does not mention SharedArrayBuffer or atomics.

**Relaxed SIMD:** Not mentioned. The page gives a general rule: "In general, Workers supports the same set of features that are available in Google Chrome."

**Loading .wasm modules:** The page does not cover `import`, `compileStreaming`, or runtime compile restrictions. It says only that "`WebAssembly.instantiate()` only supports pre-compiled modules," and points to the web-standards documentation for details.

**Size and memory:**
- "Compiling to WebAssembly often requires including additional runtime dependencies."
- "The larger your Worker is, the longer it may take your Worker to start."
- It recommends optimizing binary size with tools like `wasm-opt`.
- The page says nothing about memory limits.

The FAQ doesn't cover GPUs, max instances, linux/amd64-only support, or ingress limits. It does address these:

- **Cold starts:** "Container cold starts can often be in the 1-3 second range." The page says this varies with image size and code execution time.
- **How long instances run:** "Cloudflare does not stop a container instance after a fixed maximum runtime." Idle containers stop after inactivity, and the `Container` class defaults to 10 minutes. Platform events can also stop instances, and "Cloudflare does not guarantee that any container instance will run for a set period."
- **Egress:** The page doesn't state egress limits. It refers you to Handle outbound traffic for "how to control outbound traffic and internet access."

For GPU support, instance caps, architecture support, and ingress limits, check the Containers limits or configuration documentation.

- **Voices ready to use or make your own:** Choose from ready-to-use voices, or
  design or clone your own and bring it to your device with [two
  scripts](#voices).
- **Control the delivery:** Set the speaking rate with the `duration_delta`
  condition, and start playing streamed audio before the full utterance is ready.

## Performance

Two model sizes, one inference stack. Each cell is how many seconds of audio Phonon makes per
second of compute (higher is faster; above 1x is faster than real time) and the time to first
byte (TTFB). CPU rows use the number of cores shown; the Neural Engine row runs on the accelerator.

| Device | Phonon 31m | Phonon 40m |
|---|---|---|
| MacBook Air M5, CPU + KleidiAI, 1 core | 26x · 5 ms | 20x · 7 ms |
| MacBook Air M5, CPU + KleidiAI, 4 cores | 41x · 6 ms | 39x · 8 ms |
| iPhone 16 Pro, Neural Engine | 22x · 9 ms | 20x · 12 ms |
| Raspberry Pi 5, CPU, 1 core | 2.3x · 68 ms | 2.2x · 88 ms |

- TTFB stays under 20 ms on Apple devices, because Phonon streams frame by frame instead of waiting
  for the whole sentence.
- On one MacBook Air core, Phonon 40m reaches 20x real time with a 7 ms TTFB. Kokoro (82M), through
  its own PyTorch package on the same core, reaches 7.3x with a 776 ms TTFB, since it makes the whole
  sentence before returning any audio.

# libopus-wasm

![libopus-wasm banner](docs/assets/readme-banner.jpg)

[![CI](https://github.com/openclaw/libopus-wasm/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/openclaw/libopus-wasm/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-libopus--wasm.dev-6d4aff)](https://libopus-wasm.dev)

Small, modern WebAssembly bindings for [libopus](https://opus-codec.org/) raw
packet encode/decode. One single-file ES module that runs unchanged in browsers
and Node — no `locateFile` hook, no second `.wasm` request, no native build step.

The default path is realtime voice: 48 kHz, stereo, 20 ms frames, raw Opus
packets, no Ogg/WebM container layer.

- **Browser and Node** from one import. Bundles cleanly with Vite, webpack, esbuild.
- **Int16 and Float32 PCM** — use whatever your pipeline already speaks.
- **Loss-resilient** — in-band FEC and packet-loss concealment.
- **Tunable** — bitrate, VBR/CBR, complexity, signal, bandwidth, DTX, plus a curated CTL passthrough.
- **Drop-in `@discordjs/opus` adapter** — same method shape, no node-gyp.

📖 **Full documentation: [libopus-wasm.dev](https://libopus-wasm.dev)**

## Install

```bash
npm install libopus-wasm
```

# Can Phonon 31m run on Cloudflare? (researched 2026-10-22)

Source tags: [T] trial (npm pack of `phonon-tts@0.4.1`, read locally), [S] source (repo files, npm/ghcr registry metadata), [D] Cloudflare docs, via the docs search tool and fetches.

## A. Phonon as WebAssembly in a Worker / Workflow step

### Platform limits (Workers)
- Memory per isolate: 128 MB, Free and Paid. https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/ [D]
- CPU time per invocation: Paid default 30 s, configurable to 300,000 ms (`limits.cpu_ms`). Free is 10 ms. Waiting on network does not count. Same page [D].
- Workflow step: Paid default 30 s CPU, configurable to 5 min CPU; wall-clock per step is unlimited. https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/reference/limits/ [D]. The Workflows page says a Workflow shares the Worker's per-invocation CPU limit.
- Bundle size: 64 MiB uncompressed, all plans. The compressed-size limit (previously 3 MB Free / 10 MB Paid) was removed on 2026-09-04. https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-09-04-increased-worker-size-limit/ [D]. The Workflows limits page still lists the old 3/10 MB script size; it conflicts with the changelog and limits page.
- Startup: global scope must run in under 1 s [D].
- Static assets: 25 MiB per file, up to 100,000 files on Paid [D].
- Static assets are a place to put weights, but the limits page does not say a 64 MB file fits there. A 64.5 MB q8 GGUF is above both the 25 MiB asset limit and, with the 4.4 MB wasm, the 64 MiB bundle limit (64.5 MB ≈ 61.5 MiB; I did not test the bundle). The limits page recommends R2/KV/D1/static assets over bundling.
- WASM SIMD: "SIMD is supported on Workers." https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/webassembly/ [D]. Relaxed SIMD is not mentioned there; the page says Workers supports "the same set of features that are available in Google Chrome".
- WASM threads: "Threading is not possible in Workers." "Each Worker runs in a single thread, and the Web Worker API is not supported." Same page [D]. `SharedArrayBuffer` and atomics are not mentioned.
- `WebAssembly.instantiate()` only supports pre-compiled modules (the `.wasm` is imported as a module, not compiled from bytes at runtime). Same page [D].

### `ptts-wasm` package
- npm name `phonon-tts`, latest 0.4.1 (published 2026-10-21; `next` is 0.4.0-rc.3; first release 0.0.1 on 2026-09-23). License MIT OR Apache-2.0. Provenance attestation present. https://registry.npmjs.org/phonon-tts [S]
- Repo `gradium-ai/xn-ptts`: created 2026-05-03, last push 2026-10-21, 248 stars, not archived, Apache-2.0 (repo license field). https://github.com/gradium-ai/xn-ptts [S]
- Package size: 17.76 MB unpacked, 24 files [S]. Four wasm builds, each ~4.35–4.41 MB: `wasm/phonon_tts_bg.wasm` 4,387,050 B (Relaxed SIMD), `wasm/phonon_tts_simd_bg.wasm` 4,347,989 B (no Relaxed SIMD), and the same two under `wasm-threads/` (4,410,853 B, 4,392,191 B) [T].
- Weights are not in the package. `PhononTTS.load()` downloads weights, tokenizer, config and voices from Hugging Face (`hf://gradium/phonon-31m-en`, pinned commit) or from URLs in a `ModelSpec`, and caches them in the browser Cache API [T: README, fetch.js, hub.js]. - npm name `phonon-tts`, latest 0.4.1 (published 2026-10-21; `next` is 0.4.0-rc.3; first release 0.0.1 on 2026-09-23). License MIT OR Apache-2.0. Provenance attestation present. https://registry.npmjs.org/phonon-tts [S]
- Repo `gradium-ai/xn-ptts`: created 2026-05-03, last push 2026-10-21, 248 stars, not archived, Apache-2.0 (repo license field). https://github.com/gradium-ai/xn-ptts [S]
- Package size: 17.76 MB unpacked, 24 files [S]. Four wasm builds, each ~4.35–4.41 MB: `wasm/phonon_tts_bg.wasm` 4,387,050 B (Relaxed SIMD), `wasm/phonon_tts_simd_bg.wasm` 4,347,989 B (no Relaxed SIMD), and the same two under `wasm-threads/` (4,410,853 B, 4,392,191 B) [T].
- Weights are not in the package. `PhononTTS.load()` downloads weights, tokenizer, config and voices from Hugging Face (`hf://gradium/phonon-31m-en`, pinned commit) or from URLs in a `ModelSpec`, and caches them in the browser Cache API [T: README, fetch.js, hub.js]. The raw export `phonon-tts/raw` (`wasm/phonon_tts.js`) takes already-fetched bytes: `Model.load(weights, tokenizer, config, quant, lang, rewrites, conditions, device)` [S: ptts-wasm/README.md].
- Runtime target: browsers. The npm README says: "The model runs in a dedicated Web Worker" (created with `new Worker(...)`, uses `self.postMessage`, `navigator`, `caches`, `navigator.gpu`). The repo README says: "The package runs in browsers, not Node.js." [T/S]. The wrapper (`index.js`, `worker.js`) cannot run in Workers as shipped. The raw wasm-bindgen module is separate and takes bytes, but I did not instantiate it in Workers or Node.
- SIMD: required. "A browser without SIMD cannot load the module." Two builds, with and without Relaxed SIMD, picked by `simd.js` [T].
- Threads: optional. The threaded build (via `wasm-bindgen-rayon`, Web Workers + SharedArrayBuffer) needs a cross-origin-isolated page; otherwise the single-thread build runs. Default 3 threads [T]. The package's README does not say threads work outside browsers.
- WebGPU: optional (q8 GGUF only), device `'cpu'` by default [T].
- Published WASM speed: none found. The repo README table covers native only (31m: MacBook Air M5 1 core 26x real time, 4 cores 41x; iPhone 16 Pro Neural Engine 22x; Raspberry Pi 5 1 core 2.3x). The package README says only "q8 is noticeably faster than f32" and that speed depends on device, WebGPU and threads [S/T]. No WASM-vs-native ratio is published.
- Memory: the wasm memory of the single-thread build is not documented. Your measured native peak RSS is ~0.5 GB, which compares with the 128 MB isolate limit. I did not measure WASM memory.
- Opus/ffmpeg: not applicable to the package itself. It outputs 24 kHz mono Float32 PCM or a WAV `Blob` (`encodeWav`) [T].
- Opus in a Worker would need a separate WASM encoder. Candidates found (not tested in Workers):
  - `libopus-wasm` 0.4.1 (2026-09-24), 435 KB unpacked, single-file ES module, "runs unchanged in browsers and Node", raw Opus packets only, no Ogg container. https://registry.npmjs.org/libopus-wasm [S]
  - `@evan/opus` 1.0.3 (2024-02-11), WASM and native bindings, raw packets [S].
  - An Ogg/Opus muxer would be separate code.

## B. Cloudflare Containers running `ptts-openai-server`

### Platform
- Status: available on Workers Paid. https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/ [D]
- Instance types, https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/platform/limits/ [D]:

  | Type | vCPU | Memory | Disk |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | lite | 1/16 | 256 MiB | 2 GB |
  | basic | 1/4 | 1 GiB | 4 GB |
  | standard-1 | 1/2 | 4 GiB | 8 GB |
  | standard-2 | 1 | 6 GiB | 12 GB |
  | standard-3 | 2 | 8 GiB | 16 GB |
  | standard-4 | 4 | 12 GiB | 20 GB |

- Custom types: 1–4 vCPU, up to 12 GiB, up to 20 GB disk, at least 3 GiB memory per vCPU (disk-to-memory ratio limit removed 2026-09-29) [D].
- GPUs: no GPU instance type is listed in the limits or pricing pages, and a docs search for Containers GPU returned nothing. This is absence of evidence, not a documented statement that GPUs are unsupported.
- Architecture: image must run on `linux/amd64` [D: get-started].
- Account limits: 1,500 concurrent vCPU, 6 TiB concurrent memory, 30 TB concurrent disk, 50 GB total image storage; image size cannot exceed the instance disk size. Defaults, can be raised via support [D].
- `max_instances` is set per application in Wrangler [D]. No fixed per-application cap was found beyond the account limits.
- Cold start: "often in the 1-3 second range", depending on image size and entrypoint work. https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/faq/ [D]. This excludes model load time. Disk is ephemeral.
- Lifetime: no fixed maximum runtime; idle stop (the `Container` class defaults to 10 min); platform events can stop instances [D].
- Calling: Worker → Durable Object binding → `ctx.container` (or the `Container` class) → `container.getTcpPort(port).fetch()`. Only HTTP via the Worker; the end user cannot reach TCP/UDP directly. A Workflow step can call the Durable Object stub. Examples page lists Workflow integrations. https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/concepts/architecture/ [D]
- Pricing (Workers Paid), https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/platform/pricing/ [D]:
  - memory $0.0000025 per GiB-second beyond 25 GiB-hours/month included
  - CPU $0.000020 per vCPU-second beyond 375 vCPU-minutes/month, billed on active use only
  - disk $0.00000007 per GB-second beyond 200 GB-hours/month
  - memory and disk billed on provisioned resources, whole instance, per 10 ms while running
  - egress $0.025/GB North America & Europe (1 TB/month included), $0.05/GB Oceania, Korea, Taiwan (500 GB included), $0.04/GB elsewhere (500 GB included)
  - the Worker and a Durable Object per container are billed separately.

### `ptts-openai-server` image
- Registry: `ghcr.io/gradium-ai/ptts-openai-server`; tags `0.4.1`, `0.4.0`, `latest`, `main`, rc tags (ghcr tag list) [S].
- Architecture: `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` multi-platform manifest [S: ghcr manifest, Dockerfile]. On x86 it ships two builds (`x86-64-v3` with AVX2, `x86-64-v2` without) and a `select-cpu.sh` picks one at start [S].
- Size: amd64 compressed layers total 50.3 MB (28.2 + 3.7 + 18.3 MB), summed from the ghcr manifest. Uncompressed size not measured. The image contains no weights; it downloads the model and catalog voices from Hugging Face on first start and logs nothing until loaded. Base is `debian:bookworm-slim` with libopus0 and libmp3lame0 [S].
- API: `POST /v1/audio/speech` (OpenAI TTS-compatible). `input` up to 4096 chars, long text split at sentence ends. `voice` from `GET /v1/audio/voices` or `default`. `speed` only 1.0 (or any 0.25–4.0 ignored with `--ignore-speed`). `model`, `instructions` and `stream_format` accepted and ignored. Also `GET /v1/models` and `GET /health`; optional Wyoming protocol [S: ptts-openai-server/README.md].
- Response format: `mp3` (default), `opus`, `wav`, `pcm` (16-bit mono 24 kHz headerless). `aac` and `flac` return 400. The audio is streamed as it is generated [S]. Server-side Opus works through libopus. The README does not say whether the `opus` response is Ogg-wrapped or raw packets; I did not run it.
- Configuration (env or flags): `PTTS_LANG` (required; image defaults `en`), `PTTS_QUANT` (image defaults `q8`), `PTTS_MODEL` (folder or `hf://owner/name@sha`), `PTTS_VOICE_DIR`, `PTTS_VOICE_CATALOG`, `PTTS_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS` (default 1; extra requests get HTTP 429 `server_busy`), `PTTS_CONDITION`, `PTTS_VOICE_ALIAS`, `PTTS_OPENAI_VOICES`, `PTTS_IGNORE_SPEED`, `PTTS_WYOMING_ADDR`, `HF_TOKEN`; `--addr` default `0.0.0.0:8880` [S]. No CPU thread-count flag is documented in this README; `--help` lists more, which I did not run.
- Authentication: none ("an `Authorization` header is ignored") [S]. Access through a Worker/DO would need to be the only path.
- Phonon 31m weights license Apache 2.0 (the 40m models are CC BY-NC 4.0 and gated) [S: npm README].
- ffmpeg: not in the image. The Dockerfile installs only `ca-certificates`, `libmp3lame0`, `libopus0` [S]. A custom image could add ffmpeg; Containers accept any `linux/amd64` image within the instance disk size [D].
